All optional handouts

  1. PW-245–60 min

    The Install Fault Tree

    A layered diagnostic for separating shell, path, runtime, identity/access, local-policy, and tool failures.

    Use when
    Use when an install or smoke test fails and the next move is unclear.
    Artifact
    A reusable fault tree annotated with evidence from one real failure.
  2. PW-445–60 min

    Cold-Start Reproducibility

    A proof protocol for distinguishing durable workstation readiness from warm state and remembered fixes.

    Use when
    Use after setup appears green or before a machine is trusted for evidence-bearing work.
    Artifact
    A cold-start run record with versions, inputs, outputs, and recovery notes.
  3. P1-260–75 min

    Metamorphic Tests for Generative Judgment Products

    A practical test family for checking sensitivity, invariance, contradiction handling, and corruption response when no single oracle is enough.

    Use when
    Use when a generative product sounds plausible but exact expected output cannot be prewritten.
    Artifact
    A metamorphic test sheet with transformations, expected relations, and observed failures.
  4. P1-545–60 min

    Reproducible Runs: Stable IDs, Manifests, and Hashes

    A run-evidence pattern that binds inputs, configuration, identity, and outputs into a replayable record.

    Use when
    Use when another operator must be able to reconstruct what produced a brief or verdict.
    Artifact
    A run manifest and replay checklist for one evidence-bearing product.
  5. P2-160–75 min

    Build an Eval That Can Still Surprise You

    An eval-design method that protects coverage, hostile cases, holdouts, and the possibility of an unwelcome result.

    Use when
    Use before tuning a harness or accepting a benchmark that is easy to game.
    Artifact
    An eval charter with construct map, coverage table, holdout plan, and invalidation conditions.
  6. P2-245–60 min

    One Run Is a Probe, Not Proof

    A measurement guide for variance, repeated trials, order effects, and claims proportionate to sample size.

    Use when
    Use when a single before-and-after score is being treated as a stable capability claim.
    Artifact
    A repeated-run worksheet with variance notes and a bounded conclusion.
  7. P3-145–60 min

    Independence Is a Spectrum

    A common-mode risk map for shared prompts, context, tools, data, infrastructure, and model ancestry.

    Use when
    Use before treating agreement between engines or reviewers as independent corroboration.
    Artifact
    An independence ledger with shared-state risks and isolation moves.
  8. P3-345–60 min

    When Both Engines Agree

    A risk-based audit for correlated error hidden behind fluent agreement.

    Use when
    Use when two outputs converge and the team is tempted to treat consensus as truth.
    Artifact
    A silent-agreement audit with shared-cause hypotheses and decisive checks.
  9. P4-160–75 min

    Claim Lineage: One Rumor, Five Notes

    A lineage exercise for detecting derivative evidence, circular sourcing, and false independence in linked knowledge.

    Use when
    Use when many notes appear to support a claim but may all descend from one report.
    Artifact
    A claim-lineage graph with source roots, transformations, and confidence corrections.
  10. P4-545–60 min

    Negative Knowledge and Honest Refusal

    A practical method for representing unknown, disputed, withheld, stale, and not-yet-observed facts without filling gaps.

    Use when
    Use when a knowledge system is rewarded for answering even though the evidence cannot support an answer.
    Artifact
    A refusal and negative-knowledge schema tested against ambiguous questions.
  11. P5-360–75 min

    Proving a Negative: The Containment Evidence Ladder

    An evidence ladder for bounding claims that an untrusted input did not affect protected outputs or actions.

    Use when
    Use when containment must be demonstrated from artifacts rather than asserted from instructions.
    Artifact
    A containment proof packet with manifests, canaries, diffs, reruns, and residual uncertainty.
  12. P6-260–75 min

    From Risk List to Contract: FMEA for Agent Work

    A failure-mode analysis that turns severity, likelihood, detectability, ownership, evidence, and recovery into contract rows.

    Use when
    Use before autonomous work runs unattended or when a risk list has no enforceable owners.
    Artifact
    An FMEA-to-contract table with orphan risks exposed.
  13. P6-545–60 min

    The Human Factors of Supervising Autonomy

    A supervision field guide for mode confusion, stop reluctance, alarm fatigue, exception overload, and skill decay.

    Use when
    Use when a technically bounded system still depends on a human noticing and acting at the right time.
    Artifact
    A supervision risk map and intervention rehearsal.
  14. P7-145–60 min

    The Machine-Choice Field Manual

    A workload-sorting method using variability, volume, reversibility, latency, risk, and the value of human judgment.

    Use when
    Use before deciding whether work belongs in an agent loop, a gated pipeline, or human hands.
    Artifact
    A scored workload portfolio with routing reasons and revisit triggers.
  15. P7-460–75 min

    Human Gate Capacity and Exception Economics

    A capacity and exception-economics method for arrivals, service rate, queue age, defaults, escalation, false holds, and misses.

    Use when
    Use after a correctly placed human gate exists and its exception lane must carry real work without hiding delay or error.
    Artifact
    A gate capacity model and exception packet specification.
  16. P8-260–75 min

    Know the Endpoint Trust Boundary

    A trust-boundary map for credentials, transport, egress, logging, retention, provider access, and local control claims.

    Use when
    Use before sensitive work is pointed at a new model endpoint or hosting arrangement.
    Artifact
    An endpoint data-flow and trust-boundary record with unresolved questions made explicit.
  17. P8-560–75 min

    Capability Tax and Endpoint Portfolio

    A portfolio method for routing work across endpoints by measured capability, risk, privacy, latency, cost, resilience, and acceptable degradation.

    Use when
    Use when one endpoint cannot honestly be the best home for every workload.
    Artifact
    A workload-to-endpoint routing matrix with hold-routing and bounded-degrade rules.
  18. PC-15 min

    Operator’s Pocket Card

    A one-page field reference for the five-part brief, six-step lesson flow, evidence standard, and stop conditions.

    Use when
    Keep beside the keyboard during any evidence-bearing AI run.
    Artifact
    A printed one-page operator card.
